name: Pumpkin Cheesecake with Oatmeal-Pecan Crust & Vanilla Mascarpone Whipped Cream

instructions.primary_message: Cut cream cheese into small pieces; set aside to soften while you prepare the crust.

FOR THE CRUST: Preheat oven to 350°F. Coat the bottom and sides of a 9-inch springform pan with a thin layer of oil. Press a 10-inch circle of parchment paper into the bottom of the pan, pressing the edges firmly up the sides of the pan. Set aside.
Place oats, flour, sugar, baking soda, and salt in the bowl of a standing mixer fitted with a paddle attachment.
instructions.secondary_message:
¾ cup oats, quick cooking
¾ cup all-purpose flour
1 ½ tsp baking soda
0.06 tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Chop pecans into 1/4-inch pieces. Cut cold butter into 1/2-inch pieces. Add both to the bowl with the dry ingredients. Mix on medium-low speed until the mixture becomes moist and crumbly, 3-5 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
⅓ cup pecan halves
113 g butter, unsalted

instructions.primary_message: Transfer the oat mixture to the prepared springform pan and spread out in an even layer. Using your hands, gently press the crumb crust into the pan (do not pack down), making sure the crust is flush against the sides and corners of the pan.

Set the springform pan on top of a baking sheet pan. Place in the oven and bake until crust is a light golden color and slightly puffed, about 10 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside to cool. (Leave the oven on.)
FOR THE CHEESECAKE: While the crust is baking, wipe out the bowl of the stand mixer with paper towels.

Place the softened cream cheese and both sugars in the bowl of the standing mixer fitted with a paddle attachment. Beat on medium speed until smooth and creamy, stopping to scrape down the sides of the bowl with a silicone spatula as needed, 1-2 minutes.
Reduce mixer speed to low. Add eggs, one at a time, until just incorporated. After each addition, stop the mixer and scrape down the sides.

In a small bowl whisk together pumpkin, sour cream, cornstarch, vanilla, pumpkin pie spice, and salt. Add to the bowl with the cream cheese and mix on low speed until just combined, stopping the mixer to scrape the sides as needed. Set the cheesecake batter aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 (425 g) can pure pumpkin purée
⅓ cup sour cream
1 ½ tbsp cornstarch
1 tbsp vanilla extract
2 tsp pumpkin pie spice
¼ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Fill a large pot about halfway with hot water (from the tap); cover and bring to a boil over high heat. (This will be used for the cheesecake's hot water bath.)

Meanwhile, cut two large pieces of aluminum foil and arrange them, perpendicularly, one on top of the other. Place the springform pan in the center of the foil and carefully (making sure not to tear the foil) pull the sides up and around the outside of the pan. (This will prevent water from seeping into the pan while the cheesecake bakes.)
Place the foil-wrapped pan in the center of a large roasting dish. Pour the cheesecake batter over the crust, spreading the top out in a smooth layer.
Carefully pour the boiling water into the roasting pan (it should come about halfway up the sides of the pan).
Place cheesecake in the oven and bake, undisturbed, until firm around the edges and slightly jiggly in the center, 65-75 minutes.
When the cheesecake is done, turn off the oven. Crack the oven door just slightly (you can use a wooden spoon to keep the door slightly ajar), and allow the cheesecake to rest in the oven for 1 hour.

Carefully remove cheesecake from the water bath and place the springform pan on a cooling rack. Let cool to room temperature, then loosely cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 12 hours or overnight.

TO FINISH THE CHEESECAKE: Place cream, mascarpone cheese, sugar, and vanilla in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a whip attachment. Whip on medium-high until medium-soft peaks form. (For medium-soft peaks, when you pull the whisk out of the bowl, the cream should hold its shape, with a peak that curls over slightly.)
instructions.secondary_message:
237 ml heavy whipping cream
1 (227 g) pkg mascarpone cheese
granulated sugar
vanilla extract

instructions.primary_message: Unmold the cheesecake and place on a platter. Using a small offset spatula (or butter knife), spread a thin layer of whipped cream around the sides of the cheesecake. (Set remaining whipped cream aside.)

Chop pecans into small pieces. Using your hands, scoop up a small portion of the pecans and gently press them into the side of the cheesecake. Repeat with remaining pecans, rotating the cake as needed.

Transfer 1/3 of the remaining whipped cream to a resealable plastic bag or piping bag. Cut the tip of the bag and pipe a scalloped design around the edge of the cake. Refrigerate decorated cheesecake and remaining 2/3 of the whipped cream until ready to serve.
Cut cheesecake into 12 slices and serve with remaining whipped cream on the side. Enjoy!
